A diamond cut refers to `how well a diamond's facets interact with light to produce brilliance, fire, and sparkle`.[[1]](https://www.brilliantearth.com/en-au/diamond/buying-guide/cut/)

You can learn more about official quality standards through the [Gemological Institute of America (GIA)](https://4cs.gia.edu/en-us/diamond-cut/) or explore detailed grading criteria on the [Brilliant Earth Diamond Cut Guide](https://www.brilliantearth.com/diamond/buying-guide/cut/).[[1]](https://4cs.gia.edu/en-us/diamond-cut/)[[2]](https://www.brilliantearth.com/en-au/diamond/buying-guide/cut/)

### Cut vs. Shape

- **Cut:** Describes the symmetry, proportions, polish, and faceting design that determine how much light bounces through the stone.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diamond_cut)[[2]](https://4cs.gia.edu/en-us/diamond-cut/)[[3]](https://www.brilliantearth.com/en-au/diamond/buying-guide/cut/)
- **Shape:** Refers to the physical outline or geometric form of the diamond, such as round, oval, or pear.[[1]](https://www.tiffany.com/engagement/diamond-education/diamond-shapes.html)[[2]](https://www.brilliantearth.com/en-au/diamond/buying-guide/cut/)

### Key Cut Quality Factors

- **Brilliance:** The total amount of white light reflected from the surface and inside of a diamond.[[1]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VLCD1MsVUF8&t=69)
- **Fire:** The dispersion of white light into colorful rainbow flashes.[[1]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VLCD1MsVUF8&t=69)
- **Scintillation:** The flashes of light and dark areas (sparkle) you see when the diamond moves.[[1]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VLCD1MsVUF8&t=69)
- **Proportions:** The precise angles and relative measurements of the stone; poor proportions cause light to leak out the bottom or sides rather than reflecting back to your eye.[[1]](https://www.ritani.com/blogs/education/diamond-cut-excellent-vs-very-good)

### Popular Diamond Shapes

- **Round Brilliant:** The most popular and traditional shape, engineered for maximum sparkle.
- **Princess:** A square or rectangular shape with sharp corners and brilliant faceting.
- **Oval:** An elongated curved shape that offers a modern twist on the classic round cut.
- **Emerald:** A rectangular cut with stepped facets that create a hall-of-mirrors effect.
- **Cushion:** A square or rectangular shape with rounded corners for a soft, vintage look.[[1]](https://stienhardt.com/blogs/trends-styles/most-popular-diamond-cuts/)[[2]](https://www.tiffany.com/engagement/diamond-education/diamond-shapes.html)[[3]](https://www.zales.com/education/diamonds/shape)[[4]](https://www.google.com/search?q=product&prds=pvt:hg,productid:16776460388014835088,catalogid:36129041884644126,gpcid:3604290148667473220&ibp=oshop)[[5]](https://www.graff.com/us-en/guide-to-diamond-cuts-and-shapes.html)

expanded_element.title: Diamond Cuts Guide - Brilliant Earth
expanded_element.snippet: Cut is no different — generally, the higher the cut grade, the higher the price. Finding the right diamond is a balancing act between your budget and the 4 Cs. For example, if sparkle is the most important to you, you may need to prioritize cut and sacrifice on carat, color, or clarity to stay within budget.

items.title: How does diamond cut affect its brilliance?

expanded_element.title: Diamond Cut Guide: Understanding Cut Grade & Quality - VRAI
expanded_element.snippet: A high-quality cut invites maximum light for breathtaking brilliance, fire, and scintillation. Diamond cut influences how large, brilliant, and lustrous your diamond appears. It can make a lower-color-grade lab-grown diamond shine brighter or cause a nearly-flawless diamond to appear dull.
